skill.title: Search visible surfaces first and broaden across plausible locations
skill.principle: When a target object's location is unknown, locate it before manipulation by checking open, directly observable surfaces and common holding places first, such as tables, countertops, desks, dressers, shelves, beds, sofas, and chairs. Only then open closed containers such as drawers, cabinets, fridges, and microwaves. Treat the search as a broad multi-location search rather than assuming one named receptacle contains the object; if an early location is empty, broaden to other plausible unchecked locations.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target object's location is unknown at the start, or when the first checked location does not contain it.

skill.description: Failed searches often repeat the same empty surfaces or failed take attempts, or conclude the object is unavailable before all plausible open surfaces and relevant containers have been checked. A search should maintain a checked-location list and move to a new unchecked plausible location after a failed take.
skill.why_it_happens: The search may be treated as an unconstrained sequence without bookkeeping, so empty locations are revisited and some plausible locations are never examined.
skill.how_to_avoid: Record each checked location and its result. After a failed take or empty look, mark that location checked and move to another plausible unchecked location. Do not revisit confirmed empty surfaces unless the environment state changed. Open closed receptacles before treating them as searched and prioritize locations by object type. Search likely containers and surfaces; if the object remains absent after relevant locations are exhausted, report failure rather than continuing indefinitely.

skill.title: Open closed containers before taking or placing, and verify destination openability
skill.principle: When a closed drawer, cabinet, safe, fridge, microwave, or similar container may hold the target or is the placement destination, navigate to it and open it before attempting to take from it or put into it. Closed containers cannot be inspected or used directly. Before placing, confirm the destination is already open or can be opened; if opening returns no change, treat it as non-openable and choose a valid open destination or surface. For non-openable fixtures, use only a go-then-put sequence.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target may be inside a closed container, or when the placement destination is closed or its openability is uncertain.

skill.title: Navigate to the object and destination before take or put; proceed directly after acquisition
skill.principle: A take action succeeds only when the actor is at the receptacle where the object is present, and a put action succeeds only when the actor is at the destination. Locate and acquire the target object before traveling to the target container. Once the target is held, go directly to the specified destination and place it without unnecessary intermediate steps; if a put fails, verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying.
skill.when_to_apply: When retrieving an object whose location is not current, when moving a held object to a destination, or after a failed put.

skill.title: Use exact action forms, identifiers, and matching object types
skill.principle: Use the environment's supported action forms: go to a location, take an object from a receptacle, put an object in or on a receptacle, and open a container before accessing it. Refer to exact object and receptacle identifiers from observations, and track the specific instance taken so later actions use the same one. Do not use examine or open on non-container surfaces; open only applies to openable containers. Before taking or transforming, confirm the object name matches the goal, because similar but different objects may not satisfy it. If many containers have been checked without success, reassess visible surfaces and the target description rather than continuing blind exhaustive checks.
skill.when_to_apply: Throughout object search, retrieval, and placement, especially when forming commands or when an action seems unsupported or ambiguous.

skill.description: When an action such as go to, open, take, put, use, or clean returns 'Nothing happens', do not repeat the same command. Failed attempts can come from being at the wrong location, using an inexact or invalid identifier, targeting a closed or non-openable receptacle, or trying an inaccessible location. After a failed placement, verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying. Treat an unreachable navigation target as unavailable and switch to another candidate; treat an already-open container as open and continue rather than reopening it. Repeated no-change results are evidence that the current approach is exhausted.
skill.why_it_happens: The same invalid action may be retried without updating the inferred state, and a failed task segment may be reissued identically instead of changing the search location, object description, or strategy.
skill.how_to_avoid: After a no-change observation, re-check location, inventory, exact identifiers, and object or container state. Change at least one relevant condition: move to a different reachable location, open a closed container, use the specific instance id, or switch to another strategy. After one or two identical failures, stop retrying. If a task segment fails or returns without meeting its condition, do not repeat it unchanged; broaden the search or change the approach. Before declaring blocked, ensure every plausible closed container was actually opened and inspected, not merely approached, and avoid revisiting surfaces already confirmed empty.

skill.title: Use an acquire-then-operate sequence with explicit completion conditions
skill.principle: For tasks that require an object to be found and then manipulated, cleaned, heated, cooled, examined, or placed, split the task into an acquisition phase and an operation phase. The acquisition phase ends only when the target object is actually held, not merely seen or when a container is opened. The operation phase ends only when the environment observation confirms the required final state, such as the object being at the destination, cleaned, heated, or cooled. Begin placement only after acquisition is confirmed by holding the target object.
skill.when_to_apply: When a goal requires an object to be acquired before it is used, transformed, or placed, and the object is not already held.

skill.description: Do not declare completion or stop based on an attempted action alone. After critical actions such as take, put, clean, heat, or cool, inspect the observation for the goal predicate. Declare success only when the observation confirms the required final state; declare failure only when the observation shows an invalid or blocked action, an unreachable object, or exhaustion of plausible locations. If the placement observation already confirms the goal, treat it as terminal and do not run a redundant verification step.
skill.why_it_happens: Plans may assume an action succeeded without checking feedback, or may declare failure after a successful action sequence, or may add an unnecessary verification step after success, causing loops.
skill.how_to_avoid: After each critical action, compare the observation with the expected state. If the action failed, retry only after adjusting the approach; if it succeeded, stop issuing extra actions. Treat a confirming placement, cleaning, heating, or cooling observation as the terminal success condition. Do not declare completion before the final placement is confirmed; after confirmation, stop and do not send empty or inventory-only actions.

skill.title: Simple pick-and-place procedure
skill.principle: For simple pick-and-place goals, decompose the task into two ordered subtasks: first locate and take the target object, then move to the specified destination and put the object down.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal is to move a single object to a specified destination and no additional state change such as cleaning, heating, cooling, or lighting is required.

skill.title: 台灯观察：定位目标物与台灯并在台灯所在家具处使用台灯
skill.principle: 先确认目标物和台灯位置；台灯通常固定在家具表面。若台灯已在桌面、边桌、梳妆台等表面被观察到，直接前往该家具，不要继续搜索无关容器或盲目开抽屉。目标物不在台灯处时，先取得并携带目标物到该家具；目标物已在台灯处时，可直接尝试使用台灯，若交互未被接受再确保目标物在手中并重试。到达后使用带实例编号的 use desklamp <id> 触发观察；不要用裸名或复合语法，也不要把台灯当作可携带物或导航点。若在台灯所在家具处已取得目标物，不要再次 go to 同一位置，直接 use desklamp <id>。成功开启台灯即为终止条件，不要在其后追加 use/look。
skill.when_to_apply: 当任务要求 examine/look at 某物 with/under the desklamp，且环境中存在可交互的 desklamp 时。

skill.description: 多条失败轨迹显示，take desklamp、go to desklamp 或重复 go to 台灯/桌面通常返回 Nothing happens，浪费步骤并可能阻断后续观察。台灯是固定在家具上的交互点，不是可携带物或可导航位置。
skill.why_it_happens: 环境把台灯建模为固定光源或固定设备，只有其所在家具可作为导航目标，台灯本身不能作为 take 或 go to 的目标。
skill.how_to_avoid: 不要尝试拿取、移动或导航到台灯。先到达承载台灯的家具（desk、sidetable、dresser、coffeetable 等），在已到达后直接使用带编号的 use desklamp <id>；若已在台灯处，不要重复 go to 同一位置。

skill.description: 失败轨迹中，examine X with desklamp、examine 目标物、examine desklamp、裸名 use desklamp、use desklamp on X、use X on desklamp 常返回 There's nothing special about X 或 Nothing happens，不能替代观察条件。仅把目标物放到 desk 或 desklamp 上而不触发台灯交互，也会导致任务看似完成但环境目标未达成。
skill.why_it_happens: 环境不支持把台灯作为 examine 的工具参数，也不支持裸名或复合语法；放置动作本身不会触发观察成功条件。
skill.how_to_avoid: 把目标物定位并带到台灯所在家具后，使用观察到的带编号 lamp 实例执行 use desklamp <id>。不要用 examine X with desklamp 或复合 use 语法；若已尝试无效语法，核对台灯实例名后重试，而不是反复 examine 目标物或台灯。

skill.description: 如果 use desklamp 返回 Nothing happens，通常说明当前不在台灯所在位置或交互条件未满足；同一位置重复同一 use/examine/look 指令不会改变状态，并可能形成循环或触发保护。连续一两次失败后应停止重复。
skill.why_it_happens: 使用台灯要求与台灯所在家具同处，且错误语法或位置不会产生状态变化；把空观察误当作可重试信号会重复无效动作。
skill.how_to_avoid: 失败后先核对目标物与台灯是否在当前家具处，必要时移动到已观察到的台灯家具，改用带编号 use desklamp <id> 或先取得或保持目标物后重试；若仍无变化，改为搜索其他位置或声明无法完成，不要重复相同指令。

skill.title: 台灯观察搜索策略：优先开放表面并系统检查容器
skill.principle: 搜索目标物或台灯时，优先检查与台灯相关的开放表面，如 desk、sidetable、床头柜、床、扶手椅、咖啡桌、架子等；一旦观察到台灯，应直接前往其所在家具并在需要时使用台灯，不要继续遍历大量抽屉。若合理开放表面没有目标物，再按容器类型（drawer/cabinet）系统搜索，找到后返回台灯处。避免反复 look/examine 同一位置；没有新信息时转向其他家具或容器。'under the desklamp' 不保证目标物或台灯一定在假定位置，因此假定位置不可见时应搜索其他表面和容器。
skill.when_to_apply: 在台灯观察任务中寻找目标物或台灯，或已到达假定台灯位置但目标物或台灯不在该处、连续观察无新信息时。

skill.title: Clean-then-place ordered workflow with clean-state check
skill.principle: For goals requiring a clean object to be placed, execute distinct stages: locate and acquire the target object; bring it to a compatible cleaning fixture, preferring a sinkbasin; clean it; confirm from the observation that cleaning succeeded; then go to the destination, open it if closed, and place the object. Do not place before cleaning, and do not treat the clean step as done unless the observation confirms it. If cleaning has not succeeded, return to the cleaning stage before attempting placement. If the chosen object repeatedly fails to clean, treat it as unsuitable and switch to a likely-cleanable candidate rather than looping. Treat placement confirmation as the terminal condition, not the clean step.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal is to put a clean object in or on a specified receptacle and the object is not already clean.

skill.description: A clean action can return no effect when the object is not held or the current location is not a valid cleaning fixture. Cleaning is reliably supported at a sinkbasin; alternative fixtures such as bathtubbasin or fridge should not be assumed equivalent. Repeated identical attempts waste steps.
skill.why_it_happens: The environment validates that the object is held and that cleaning occurs at a compatible fixture; some fixtures or objects do not support cleaning.
skill.how_to_avoid: Hold the target object, navigate to a sinkbasin, then clean. If no effect, verify the held object and current location; try a different sinkbasin or confirm the object is cleanable. Treat bathtubbasin as unverified and switch to sinkbasin if it fails; do not loop on an invalid fixture.

skill.description: Certain objects such as towels or cloth may not support the clean action at a sinkbasin; repeated clean attempts fail. Prefer objects that are typically cleanable, and if a clean attempt fails, consider that the chosen object may be unsuitable.
skill.why_it_happens: Not every object type supports cleaning, or the selected object may not be the task's intended cleanable item.
skill.how_to_avoid: Before committing, select a likely cleanable candidate. If clean returns no effect after confirming the fixture and held object, try another candidate object or report the object as not cleanable rather than repeating the same action.

skill.description: Placement can fail when the destination container is closed, has no available space, or is not a valid receptacle; for example, some fixtures such as toilets or coffeemachines may reject placement. An open action may also return no effect if the container is already open or not openable.
skill.why_it_happens: Containers may require opening or have capacity limits; some fixtures are not valid placement targets. Repeating put or open without changing conditions may waste steps.
skill.how_to_avoid: Before placing, open a closed destination; if open returns no effect, do not retry it—proceed or reassess. Check for space or availability when possible. If the destination is invalid or put repeatedly has no effect, seek an alternative valid destination or report blocked rather than looping.

skill.description: Goals name a specific object type. Similar alternatives, such as mug for cup, pan for pot, or butterknife for knife, should not be silently substituted. A close synonym may be considered only if the exact object is unavailable and the environment or observation explicitly treats it as equivalent or the goal permits it; otherwise continue searching or report the mismatch.
skill.why_it_happens: Generalizing categories can cause taking the wrong item and failing the task; conversely, exact-name matching may miss an accepted synonym, so equivalence must be confirmed rather than assumed.
skill.how_to_avoid: First search for the exact named type. If not found, do not swap in a different type by default; only use a confirmed equivalent. If the destination already contains a similar object, still acquire, clean, and place the correct target rather than swapping.

skill.description: Searching for the target object should prioritize plausible locations and avoid opening every remaining container indefinitely. If the object is not found after checking a reasonable set of likely locations, reassess or report blocked rather than continuing a step-consuming loop.
skill.why_it_happens: Item locations follow some regularities, but unusual placement or impossible tasks can occur; unbounded search wastes steps and can cause timeout or failure.
skill.how_to_avoid: Prioritize likely locations by object type: food-related items in fridge; dishes or utensils in countertop, cabinet, or drawer; cleaning supplies near sinkbasin, countertop, or shelf. After a few likely locations fail, consider unusual placement or impossibility, then reassess or report blocked rather than exhaustively opening all containers.

skill.title: End-to-end heat-then-place sequence
skill.principle: For a heat-then-place goal: locate and take the target object, go to the microwave, open it if closed, perform the heating operation using an observation-confirmed method, keep track of the same object instance, then go to the final destination, open it if needed, put the object there, and confirm placement. Treat heating as an intermediate milestone; the task is complete only after the object is placed at the destination. If the object is already held after acquisition, proceed to the heating stage rather than restarting unnecessarily. Only take the object from the microwave if it was actually placed inside; if heating was done while holding, keep holding and go directly to the destination.
skill.when_to_apply: Any task requiring an object to be heated and then placed at a specified destination.

skill.title: Microwave heating with observation-driven holding/placement recovery
skill.principle: Open the microwave before taking from or using it, and keep it open until heating is confirmed. Use the explicit heat action form heat <object> with microwave <id> rather than generic use <object> or use microwave. Observations conflict on the required heating state: some successful runs heated the object while holding it, while others succeeded by placing the object in an open microwave and then heating. Treat the holding/placement requirement as observation-dependent. If heating while holding returns 'Nothing happens', place the object in the open microwave and retry. If heating with the object inside returns 'Nothing happens', take it out, ensure the microwave is open, and retry while holding it. Do not repeat an identical failing heat command without changing the object’s position or holding state. Only proceed to the destination after an observation confirms the object was heated.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target object must be heated with a microwave, especially if the first heat attempt fails or the object is inside the microwave.

skill.description: A heat command can fail or return 'Nothing happens', and treating an unconfirmed attempt as success can lead to moving and placing a cold object. Do not infer heating success from merely holding or placing the object.
skill.why_it_happens: Heating may not change state unless the object’s position and the microwave state are suitable, and success is not guaranteed just because a command was issued.
skill.how_to_avoid: Proceed only after an explicit heating-success observation, such as a message that the object was heated, or another reliable confirmation that it is hot. If heating is not confirmed, repeat a valid heating attempt after correcting the object’s position or holding state, then verify again before moving it.

skill.description: After microwave heating returns 'Nothing happens', switching to stoveburners, toasters, or other appliances without evidence can also fail or be blocked. Assumption-based substitution adds failed steps rather than recovering the task.
skill.why_it_happens: Some appliances may not support heating the target object, some surfaces may be occupied, and support for a given object or appliance is not guaranteed merely because an alternative exists.
skill.how_to_avoid: Correct the microwave interaction first: check that it is open, adjust whether the object is held or placed inside, and retry without repeating the identical failing command. Use another appliance only when current observations explicitly show that it supports heating this object and is available; otherwise do not treat stoveburner or toaster as a blind fallback.

skill.title: Systematic search and continue after misses
skill.principle: When the target object is not in the first searched location, continue systematically checking other plausible containers and surfaces such as cabinets, drawers, countertops, dining table, fridge, sink basin, coffee machine, and stoveburners. Prioritize visible surfaces and high-probability containers by object type before opening every cabinet in sequence, and track checked locations to avoid redundant loops. Do not declare the task blocked or the object unavailable merely because the first location is empty.
skill.when_to_apply: During the acquisition phase of a heat-and-place task when the target object is not immediately visible or is absent from the first checked location.

skill.description: When heating succeeds while the object is held, the object remains in inventory. Attempting afterward to take it from the microwave can return 'Nothing happens' because the direct heat action did not put it there.
skill.why_it_happens: The heating action confirmed while holding the object does not necessarily move the object into the microwave, so there is nothing to take out afterward.
skill.how_to_avoid: After a successful heat action performed while holding the object, verify by inventory or held-object state that it is still held, then proceed toward the destination. Do not issue a take-from-microwave action unless the object was actually placed inside.

skill.description: Inserting an extra countertop or other intermediate placement between heating and the final destination adds unnecessary actions and can cause tracking or placement failures.
skill.why_it_happens: The task may be over-decomposed so that an intermediate placement is introduced even though the goal only requires moving the heated object to its final destination.
skill.how_to_avoid: After heating, take or keep the object and move directly to the final destination, then place it there. Add an intermediate placement only if the environment explicitly requires it.

skill.title: Cooling workflow with confirmed cool state before placement
skill.principle: Inputs differ on whether cooling requires placing the object in the fridge and taking it out or issuing an explicit cool action while holding it at an open fridge. Use environment feedback as authority: perform or verify cooling explicitly, and do not treat mere containment or brief placement as confirmed cooling. A reliable sequence is: acquire the exact target; go to the fridge; open it; if an explicit cool action is available, issue it while holding the object, otherwise use the available cooling interaction and wait for a cooled-state confirmation; then go to the destination; open it if closed; put the object there; confirm placement. Do not issue a cool action before the object is actually held. Do not add a take-from-fridge step when cooling was done while holding, and do not immediately re-take an object already held; check inventory before re-taking.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal requires an object to be cooled and then placed at a specified destination.

skill.description: An object found in the fridge, or briefly placed into it, is not guaranteed to be in the required cooled state. Cooling should be performed or verified explicitly before the object is taken to the destination.
skill.why_it_happens: The agent may conflate storage location or containment with temperature state, or may assume that a fridge round-trip is sufficient cooling. The environment may only change temperature through an explicit cool interaction.
skill.how_to_avoid: Do not immediately retrieve and place an object after putting it into the fridge. While holding the target at an open fridge, use the environment's cool interaction and wait for a confirmation. If no cooled-state confirmation occurs, do not assume success.

skill.title: Bounded systematic search and early feasibility reassessment
skill.principle: Check a few high-probability locations first, including the fridge, countertops, dining table, cabinets, drawers, and shelves. Open containers as needed and track visited locations to avoid redundant loops. If the target is not found after a reasonable broad search, reassess the goal or whether the object may be absent rather than continuing through every unrelated receptacle. Do not repeat an identical broad search after all obvious receptacles have been exhausted; report or escalate early when feasibility is doubtful.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target object is not immediately visible or is missing from its expected location, and many storage receptacles exist.

skill.description: Omitting the cooling phase and placing the object directly, or stopping after opening the fridge or cooling the object without final placement, leaves the goal incomplete. The task requires both a cooled object and placement at the required destination.
skill.why_it_happens: The goal may be misread as a simple placement task, or the cooling step may be treated as the whole mission. Premature handoff after a partial step also causes failure.
skill.how_to_avoid: Treat cooling and final placement as separate checkpoints. Include an explicit cooling step before placement when the goal requires a cool object, and after cooling continue to the destination and place the object. Do not declare success or hand off until both the cooled state and destination placement have been confirmed.

skill.title: Sequential two-item placement with per-item confirmation
skill.principle: Treat a two-item placement goal as two search-and-place cycles. Locate and take one target object, navigate to the destination, open the destination if it is closed, place the object, and confirm the placement before starting the second cycle. Track how many items are placed and which object was already placed; never take an already-placed object again. If both instances are visible on the same surface or receptacle, place the first then return to that same location for the second. Continue until both instances are confirmed placed; do not stop after placing only one. If the final destination is temporarily unavailable, only use a safe recoverable holding location when necessary and move both objects to the final destination afterward.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal requires placing two instances of the same object type at one target location and only one object can be carried at a time.

skill.title: Systematic search across receptacle types and visible surfaces
skill.principle: When target objects are not immediately visible, search broadly instead of checking only one receptacle type. Inspect visible surfaces such as counters, tables, shelves, sofas, dressers, and similar open surfaces first, then check closed containers such as cabinets and drawers, opening them before inspecting or taking from inside. Continue across multiple location types until the required number of instances is found or a checked-location record shows no remaining unchecked likely locations. Do not conclude the task is blocked prematurely, and do not accept a similar-named substitute for the exact target object type.
skill.when_to_apply: When one or both target objects are not visible and must be located in the environment.

skill.description: Attempts to take a second object, or sometimes to move to another location, while already holding an object can return a no-op. This blocks progress in two-item placement if the held object is not released first.
skill.why_it_happens: The environment commonly allows carrying only one object at a time, so take or movement actions may be rejected while inventory is occupied.
skill.how_to_avoid: Before taking the second object or moving to search elsewhere, put the held object into the final destination or into a safe recoverable temporary location. Confirm the hands are empty, then continue.

skill.description: A put action can produce no effect if it is issued before reaching the destination receptacle, or it can fail without the failure being noticed. Continuing to search for the second item after an unconfirmed first placement can leave the goal unsatisfied.
skill.why_it_happens: Placement requires being at the target container and a successful put must be verified from the observation; otherwise the first item may still be held or not placed.
skill.how_to_avoid: Navigate to the destination before placing. After each put, inspect the observation to confirm success. If the put did not succeed, move to the target if needed and retry before starting the next search or placement cycle. Track that the first item was already placed and drive directly to the second acquisition and final put.

skill.description: Attempting to put an object into, or take an object from, a closed cabinet, drawer, or similar container may produce no effect.
skill.why_it_happens: The environment requires the container to be open before its contents can be accessed or modified.
skill.how_to_avoid: Open the container first with the appropriate open action. If it is already open, proceed; after opening, verify access before taking or placing.

skill.description: Using an examine-style action on objects or locations is not supported and returns no useful information.
skill.why_it_happens: The available interaction set is limited to navigation, taking, putting, opening, and inventory-style operations; examining is not an effective substitute.
skill.how_to_avoid: Inspect a location by navigating to the receptacle and observing its contents. Pick up visible target objects with a take action from that receptacle.

skill.description: Placing an object into a non-target or unsuitable container such as a garbage can can make retrieval impossible or cause the overall two-item placement to fail.
skill.why_it_happens: Some containers may not accept objects cleanly, may change object state, or may not allow reliable retrieval; temporary storage is only safe if the object can be taken back.
skill.how_to_avoid: Prefer placing the first object directly into the final destination. If temporary holding is unavoidable, choose an open, stable, recoverable surface or container and avoid garbage cans or other likely irreversible containers.

skill.description: After several containers have been opened and no target found, repeatedly revisiting locations already confirmed empty can exhaust the action budget and cause failure.
skill.why_it_happens: Searching without tracking checked locations leads to redundant actions, while unchecked opened containers or visible surfaces may still contain the target.
skill.how_to_avoid: Maintain a mental or explicit list of checked locations. Prioritize unchecked opened containers and visible surfaces; take a target directly if it is visible. Avoid revisiting a location already confirmed to have no target unless new evidence suggests otherwise.

skill.description: Repeatedly declaring a subtask complete without executing the required next action can trigger a loop guard and terminate the episode before the two items are placed.
skill.why_it_happens: The current state may be misread as satisfying the completion condition even though the actual goal or subgoal is unfinished, causing repeated signals instead of progress.
skill.how_to_avoid: Signal completion only after the corresponding subgoal is actually achieved, such as an object being taken or placed. After signaling, continue with the necessary next action and avoid repeating the same completion signal without new progress.

skill.title: Search visible surfaces first and broaden across plausible locations
skill.principle: When a target object's location is unknown, locate it before manipulation by checking open, directly observable surfaces and common holding places first, such as tables, countertops, desks, dressers, shelves, beds, sofas, and chairs. Only then open closed containers such as drawers, cabinets, fridges, and microwaves. Treat the search as a broad multi-location search rather than assuming one named receptacle contains the object; if an early location is empty, broaden to other plausible unchecked locations.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target object's location is unknown at the start, or when the first checked location does not contain it.

skill.description: Failed searches often repeat the same empty surfaces or failed take attempts, or conclude the object is unavailable before all plausible open surfaces and relevant containers have been checked. A search should maintain a checked-location list and move to a new unchecked plausible location after a failed take.
skill.why_it_happens: The search may be treated as an unconstrained sequence without bookkeeping, so empty locations are revisited and some plausible locations are never examined.
skill.how_to_avoid: Record each checked location and its result. After a failed take or empty look, mark that location checked and move to another plausible unchecked location. Do not revisit confirmed empty surfaces unless the environment state changed. Open closed receptacles before treating them as searched and prioritize locations by object type. Search likely containers and surfaces; if the object remains absent after relevant locations are exhausted, report failure rather than continuing indefinitely.

skill.title: Open closed containers before taking or placing, and verify destination openability
skill.principle: When a closed drawer, cabinet, safe, fridge, microwave, or similar container may hold the target or is the placement destination, navigate to it and open it before attempting to take from it or put into it. Closed containers cannot be inspected or used directly. Before placing, confirm the destination is already open or can be opened; if opening returns no change, treat it as non-openable and choose a valid open destination or surface. For non-openable fixtures, use only a go-then-put sequence.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target may be inside a closed container, or when the placement destination is closed or its openability is uncertain.

skill.title: Navigate to the object and destination before take or put; proceed directly after acquisition
skill.principle: A take action succeeds only when the actor is at the receptacle where the object is present, and a put action succeeds only when the actor is at the destination. Locate and acquire the target object before traveling to the target container. Once the target is held, go directly to the specified destination and place it without unnecessary intermediate steps; if a put fails, verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying.
skill.when_to_apply: When retrieving an object whose location is not current, when moving a held object to a destination, or after a failed put.

skill.title: Use exact action forms, identifiers, and matching object types
skill.principle: Use the environment's supported action forms: go to a location, take an object from a receptacle, put an object in or on a receptacle, and open a container before accessing it. Refer to exact numbered object and receptacle identifiers from observations, and track the specific instance taken so later actions use the same one. Do not use examine or open on non-container surfaces; open only applies to openable containers. Before taking or transforming, confirm the object name matches the goal, because similar but different objects may not satisfy it. If many containers have been checked without success, reassess visible surfaces and the target description rather than continuing blind exhaustive checks.
skill.when_to_apply: Throughout object search, retrieval, and placement, especially when forming commands or when an action seems unsupported or ambiguous.

skill.description: When an action such as go to, open, take, put, use, or clean returns 'Nothing happens', do not repeat the same command. Failed attempts can come from being at the wrong location, using an inexact or invalid identifier, targeting a closed or non-openable receptacle, or trying an inaccessible location. After a failed placement, verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying. Treat an unreachable navigation target as unavailable and switch to another candidate; treat an already-open container as open and continue rather than reopening it. Repeated no-change results are evidence that the current approach is exhausted.
skill.why_it_happens: The same invalid action may be retried without updating the inferred state, and a failed task segment may be reissued identically instead of changing the search location, object description, or strategy.
skill.how_to_avoid: After a no-change observation, re-check location, inventory, exact identifiers, and object or container state. Change at least one relevant condition: move to a different reachable location, open a closed container, use the specific instance id, or switch to another strategy. After one or two identical failures, stop retrying. If a task segment fails or returns without meeting its condition, do not repeat it unchanged; broaden the search or change the approach. Before declaring blocked, ensure every plausible closed container was actually opened and inspected, not merely approached, and avoid revisiting surfaces already confirmed empty.

skill.title: Use an acquire-then-operate sequence with explicit completion conditions
skill.principle: For tasks that require an object to be found and then manipulated, cleaned, heated, cooled, examined, or placed, split the task into an acquisition phase and an operation phase. The acquisition phase ends only when the target object is actually held, not merely seen or when a container is opened. The operation phase ends only when the environment observation confirms the required final state, such as the object being at the destination, cleaned, heated, or cooled. Begin placement only after acquisition is confirmed by holding the target object.
skill.when_to_apply: When a goal requires an object to be acquired before it is used, transformed, or placed, and the object is not already held.

skill.description: Do not declare completion or stop based on an attempted action alone. After critical actions such as take, put, clean, heat, or cool, inspect the observation for the goal predicate. Declare success only when the observation confirms the required final state; declare failure only when the observation shows an invalid or blocked action, an unreachable object, or exhaustion of plausible locations. If the placement observation already confirms the goal, treat it as terminal and do not run a redundant verification step.
skill.why_it_happens: Plans may assume an action succeeded without checking feedback, or may declare failure after a successful action sequence, or may add an unnecessary verification step after success, causing loops.
skill.how_to_avoid: After each critical action, compare the observation with the expected state. If the action failed, retry only after adjusting the approach; if it succeeded, stop issuing extra actions. Treat a confirming placement, cleaning, heating, or cooling observation as the terminal success condition. Do not declare completion before the final placement is confirmed; after confirmation, stop and do not send empty or inventory-only actions.

skill.title: Simple pick-and-place procedure
skill.principle: For simple pick-and-place goals, decompose the task into two ordered subtasks: first locate and take the target object, then move to the specified destination and put the object down.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal is to move a single object to a specified destination and no additional state change such as cleaning, heating, cooling, or lighting is required.

skill.title: 台灯观察：定位目标物与台灯并在台灯所在家具处使用台灯
skill.principle: 先确认目标物和台灯位置；台灯通常固定在家具表面。若台灯已在桌面、边桌、梳妆台等表面被观察到，直接前往该家具，不要继续搜索无关容器。目标物不在台灯处时，先取得并携带目标物到该家具；目标物已在台灯处时，可直接尝试使用台灯，若交互未被接受再确保目标物在手中并重试。到达后使用带实例编号的 use desklamp <id> 触发观察；不要用裸名或复合语法，也不要把台灯当作可携带物或导航点。
skill.when_to_apply: 当任务要求 examine/look at 某物 with/under the desklamp，且环境中存在可交互的 desklamp 时。

skill.description: 多条失败轨迹显示，take desklamp、go to desklamp 或重复 go to 台灯/桌面通常返回 Nothing happens，浪费步骤并可能阻断后续观察。台灯是固定在家具上的交互点，不是可携带物或可导航位置。
skill.why_it_happens: 环境把台灯建模为固定光源或固定设备，只有其所在家具可作为导航目标，台灯本身不能作为 take 或 go to 的目标。
skill.how_to_avoid: 不要尝试拿取、移动或导航到台灯。先到达承载台灯的家具（desk、sidetable、dresser、coffeetable 等），在已到达后直接使用带编号的 use desklamp <id>；若已在台灯处，不要重复 go to 同一位置。

skill.description: Failed trajectories show that examine X with desklamp, examine the target, examine desklamp, bare-name use desklamp, use desklamp on X, and use X on desklamp often return 'There's nothing special about X' or 'Nothing happens' and cannot substitute for the observation condition. Merely placing the target on the desk or desklamp without triggering the lamp interaction also leaves the environment goal unmet. The working form is the numbered lamp instance, e.g. 'use desklamp 1'; bare 'use desklamp', 'use lamp', 'use desk 1', and 'open desk 1' all returned Nothing happens before the numbered form succeeded.
skill.why_it_happens: The environment does not support the desklamp as an examine tool argument, nor bare-name or compound syntax; placement actions alone do not trigger the observation success condition.
skill.how_to_avoid: After locating and bringing the target to the lamp's furniture, execute 'use desklamp <id>' with the observed numbered lamp instance. Do not use examine X with desklamp or compound use syntax; if an invalid syntax was tried, verify the lamp instance name and retry with the numbered form rather than repeatedly examining the target or lamp.

skill.description: 如果 use desklamp 返回 Nothing happens，通常说明当前不在台灯所在位置或交互条件未满足；同一位置重复同一 use/examine/look 指令不会改变状态，并可能形成循环或触发保护。连续一两次失败后应停止重复。
skill.why_it_happens: 使用台灯要求与台灯所在家具同处，且错误语法或位置不会产生状态变化；把空观察误当作可重试信号会重复无效动作。
skill.how_to_avoid: 失败后先核对目标物与台灯是否在当前家具处，必要时移动到已观察到的台灯家具，改用带编号 use desklamp <id> 或先取得或保持目标物后重试；若仍无变化，改为搜索其他位置或声明无法完成，不要重复相同指令。

skill.title: 台灯观察搜索策略：优先开放表面并系统检查容器
skill.principle: 搜索目标物或台灯时，优先检查与台灯相关的开放表面，如 desk、sidetable、床头柜、床等；一旦观察到台灯，应直接前往其所在家具并在需要时使用台灯，不要继续遍历大量抽屉。若合理开放表面没有目标物，再按容器类型（drawer/cabinet）系统搜索，找到后返回台灯处。避免反复 look/examine 同一位置；没有新信息时转向其他家具或容器。'under the desklamp' 不保证目标物或台灯一定在假定位置，因此假定位置不可见时应搜索其他表面和容器。
skill.when_to_apply: 在台灯观察任务中寻找目标物或台灯，或已到达假定台灯位置但目标物或台灯不在该处、连续观察无新信息时。

skill.title: Clean-then-place ordered workflow with clean-state check
skill.principle: For goals requiring a clean object to be placed, execute distinct stages: locate and acquire the target object; bring it to a compatible cleaning fixture, preferring a sinkbasin; clean it; confirm from the observation that cleaning succeeded; then go to the destination, open it if closed, and place the object. Do not place before cleaning, and do not treat the clean step as done unless the observation confirms it. If cleaning has not succeeded, return to the cleaning stage before attempting placement.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal is to put a clean object in or on a specified receptacle and the object is not already clean.

skill.description: A clean action can return no effect when the object is not held, the current location is not a valid cleaning fixture, or the chosen object is not cleanable (e.g., a towel or cloth may not support cleaning at a sinkbasin). Cleaning is reliably supported at a sinkbasin; alternative fixtures such as bathtubbasin or fridge should not be assumed equivalent. Repeated identical attempts waste steps, and attempting to take another object while still holding the failed one produces repeated no-ops.
skill.why_it_happens: The environment validates that the object is held and that cleaning occurs at a compatible fixture; some fixtures or object types do not support cleaning.
skill.how_to_avoid: Hold the target object, navigate to a sinkbasin, then clean. If no effect, verify the held object and current location; try a different sinkbasin or confirm the object is cleanable. After a failed clean, either try a different cleanable candidate or release the held object at a valid surface before acquiring another. Treat bathtubbasin as unverified and switch to sinkbasin if it fails; do not loop on an invalid fixture.

skill.description: Certain objects such as towels or cloth may not support the clean action at a sinkbasin; repeated clean attempts fail. Prefer objects that are typically cleanable, and if a clean attempt fails, consider that the chosen object may be unsuitable.
skill.why_it_happens: Not every object type supports cleaning, or the selected object may not be the task's intended cleanable item.
skill.how_to_avoid: Before committing, select a likely cleanable candidate. If clean returns no effect after confirming the fixture and held object, try another candidate object or report the object as not cleanable rather than repeating the same action.

skill.description: Placement can fail when the destination container is closed, has no available space, or is not a valid receptacle; for example, fixtures such as toilets or coffeemachines may reject placement, and repeated put/open/use on a coffeemachine all return 'Nothing happens'. An open action may also return no effect if the container is already open or not openable; in that case proceed to put rather than retrying open.
skill.why_it_happens: Containers may require opening or have capacity limits; some fixtures are not valid placement targets. Repeating put or open without changing conditions may waste steps.
skill.how_to_avoid: Before placing, open a closed destination; if open returns no effect, do not retry it—proceed or reassess. Check for space or availability when possible. If the destination is invalid or put repeatedly has no effect, treat it as invalid and seek an alternative valid destination or report blocked rather than looping.

skill.description: Goals name a specific object type. Similar alternatives, such as mug for cup, pan for pot, or butterknife for knife, should not be silently substituted. A close synonym may be considered only if the exact object is unavailable and the environment or observation explicitly treats it as equivalent or the goal permits it; otherwise continue searching or report the mismatch.
skill.why_it_happens: Generalizing categories can cause taking the wrong item and failing the task; conversely, exact-name matching may miss an accepted synonym, so equivalence must be confirmed rather than assumed.
skill.how_to_avoid: First search for the exact named type. If not found, do not swap in a different type by default; only use a confirmed equivalent. If the destination already contains a similar object, still acquire, clean, and place the correct target rather than swapping.

skill.description: Searching for the target object should prioritize plausible locations and avoid opening every remaining container indefinitely. If the object is not found after checking a reasonable set of likely locations, reassess or report blocked rather than continuing a step-consuming loop.
skill.why_it_happens: Item locations follow some regularities, but unusual placement or impossible tasks can occur; unbounded search wastes steps and can cause timeout or failure.
skill.how_to_avoid: Prioritize likely locations by object type: food-related items in fridge; dishes or utensils in countertop, cabinet, or drawer; cleaning supplies near sinkbasin, countertop, or shelf. After a few likely locations fail, consider unusual placement or impossibility, then reassess or report blocked rather than exhaustively opening all containers.

skill.title: End-to-end heat-then-place sequence
skill.principle: For a heat-then-place goal: locate and take the target object, go to the microwave, open it if closed, perform the heating operation using an observation-confirmed method, keep track of the same object instance, then go to the final destination, open it if needed, put the object there, and confirm placement. Treat heating as an intermediate milestone; the task is complete only after the object is placed at the destination. If the object is already held after acquisition, proceed to the heating stage rather than restarting unnecessarily.
skill.when_to_apply: Any task requiring an object to be heated and then placed at a specified destination.

skill.title: Microwave heating with explicit heat command and observation-driven recovery
skill.principle: Open the microwave before taking from or using it. Use the explicit heating command form 'heat <object> <id> with microwave <id>' while holding the object at an open microwave; bare 'use <object>' or 'use microwave <id>' are invalid forms that return 'Nothing happens'. If the explicit heat command fails while holding, place the object in the open microwave and retry the explicit heat command. If heating with the object inside fails, take it out, ensure the microwave is open, and retry while holding it. Do not repeat an identical failing heat command without changing the object's position, holding state, or command form.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target object must be heated with a microwave, especially if the first heat attempt fails or the object is inside the microwave.

skill.description: A heat command can fail or return 'Nothing happens', and treating an unconfirmed attempt as success can lead to moving and placing a cold object. Do not infer heating success from merely holding or placing the object.
skill.why_it_happens: Heating may not change state unless the object’s position and the microwave state are suitable, and success is not guaranteed just because a command was issued.
skill.how_to_avoid: Proceed only after an explicit heating-success observation, such as a message that the object was heated, or another reliable confirmation that it is hot. If heating is not confirmed, repeat a valid heating attempt after correcting the object’s position or holding state, then verify again before moving it.

skill.description: After microwave heating returns 'Nothing happens', switching to stoveburners, toasters, or other appliances without evidence can also fail or be blocked. Assumption-based substitution adds failed steps rather than recovering the task.
skill.why_it_happens: Some appliances may not support heating the target object, some surfaces may be occupied, and support for a given object or appliance is not guaranteed merely because an alternative exists.
skill.how_to_avoid: Correct the microwave interaction first: check that it is open, adjust whether the object is held or placed inside, and retry without repeating the identical failing command. Use another appliance only when current observations explicitly show that it supports heating this object and is available; otherwise do not treat stoveburner or toaster as a blind fallback.

skill.title: Systematic search and continue after misses
skill.principle: When the target object is not in the first searched location, continue systematically checking other plausible containers and surfaces such as cabinets, drawers, countertops, fridge, dining table, sink basin, coffee machine, and stoveburners. Do not declare the task blocked or the object unavailable merely because the first location is empty.
skill.when_to_apply: During the acquisition phase of a heat-and-place task when the target object is not immediately visible or is absent from the first checked location.

skill.description: When heating succeeds while the object is held, the object remains in inventory. Attempting afterward to take it from the microwave can return 'Nothing happens' because the direct heat action did not put it there.
skill.why_it_happens: The heating action confirmed while holding the object does not necessarily move the object into the microwave, so there is nothing to take out afterward.
skill.how_to_avoid: After a successful heat action performed while holding the object, verify by inventory or held-object state that it is still held, then proceed toward the destination. Do not issue a take-from-microwave action unless the object was actually placed inside.

skill.description: Inserting an extra countertop or other intermediate placement between heating and the final destination adds unnecessary actions and can cause tracking or placement failures.
skill.why_it_happens: The task may be over-decomposed so that an intermediate placement is introduced even though the goal only requires moving the heated object to its final destination.
skill.how_to_avoid: After heating, take or keep the object and move directly to the final destination, then place it there. Add an intermediate placement only if the environment explicitly requires it.

skill.title: Cooling workflow with explicit cool command and confirmed cool state before placement
skill.principle: Use environment feedback as authority and perform cooling explicitly. A reliable sequence is: acquire the exact target; go to the fridge; open it; issue the explicit cool command 'cool <object> <id> with fridge <id>' while holding the object; wait for a cooled-state confirmation; then go to the destination; open it if closed; put the object there; confirm placement. Do not treat mere containment or brief placement in the fridge as confirmed cooling, and do not immediately re-take an object already held; check inventory before re-taking. After a successful cool action while holding the object, the object remains in inventory, so proceed directly to the destination rather than trying to take it from the fridge.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal requires an object to be cooled and then placed at a specified destination.

skill.description: An object found in the fridge, or briefly placed into it, is not guaranteed to be in the required cooled state. Cooling should be performed or verified explicitly before the object is taken to the destination.
skill.why_it_happens: The agent may conflate storage location or containment with temperature state, or may assume that a fridge round-trip is sufficient cooling. The environment may only change temperature through an explicit cool interaction.
skill.how_to_avoid: Do not immediately retrieve and place an object after putting it into the fridge. While holding the target at an open fridge, use the environment's cool interaction and wait for a confirmation. If no cooled-state confirmation occurs, do not assume success.

skill.title: Bounded systematic search and early feasibility reassessment
skill.principle: Check a few high-probability locations first, including the fridge, countertops, dining table, cabinets, drawers, and shelves. Open containers as needed and track visited locations to avoid redundant loops. If the target is not found after a reasonable broad search, reassess the goal or whether the object may be absent rather than continuing through every unrelated receptacle. Do not repeat an identical broad search after all obvious receptacles have been exhausted; report or escalate early when feasibility is doubtful.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target object is not immediately visible or is missing from its expected location, and many storage receptacles exist.

skill.description: Omitting the cooling phase and placing the object directly, or stopping after opening the fridge or cooling the object without final placement, leaves the goal incomplete. The task requires both a cooled object and placement at the required destination.
skill.why_it_happens: The goal may be misread as a simple placement task, or the cooling step may be treated as the whole mission. Premature handoff after a partial step also causes failure.
skill.how_to_avoid: Treat cooling and final placement as separate checkpoints. Include an explicit cooling step before placement when the goal requires a cool object, and after cooling continue to the destination and place the object. Do not declare success or hand off until both the cooled state and destination placement have been confirmed.

skill.title: Sequential two-item placement with per-item confirmation
skill.principle: Treat a two-item placement goal as two search-and-place cycles. Locate and take one target object, navigate to the destination, open the destination if it is closed, place the object, and confirm the placement before starting the second cycle. Track how many items are placed and which object was already placed; never take an already-placed object again. If both instances are visible on the same surface or receptacle, place the first then return to that same location for the second. If the final destination is temporarily unavailable, only use a safe recoverable holding location when necessary and move both objects to the final destination afterward.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal requires placing two instances of the same object type at one target location and only one object can be carried at a time.

skill.title: Systematic search across receptacle types and visible surfaces
skill.principle: When target objects are not immediately visible, search broadly instead of checking only one receptacle type. Inspect visible surfaces such as counters, tables, shelves, sofas, and similar open surfaces first, then check closed containers such as cabinets and drawers, opening them before inspecting or taking from inside. Continue across multiple location types until the required number of instances is found or a checked-location record shows no remaining unchecked likely locations. Do not conclude the task is blocked prematurely.
skill.when_to_apply: When one or both target objects are not visible and must be located in the environment.

skill.description: Attempts to take a second object, or sometimes to move to another location, while already holding an object can return a no-op. This blocks progress in two-item placement if the held object is not released first.
skill.why_it_happens: The environment commonly allows carrying only one object at a time, so take or movement actions may be rejected while inventory is occupied.
skill.how_to_avoid: Before taking the second object or moving to search elsewhere, put the held object into the final destination or into a safe recoverable temporary location. Confirm the hands are empty, then continue.

skill.description: A put action can produce no effect if it is issued before reaching the destination receptacle, or it can fail without the failure being noticed. Continuing to search for the second item after an unconfirmed first placement can leave the goal unsatisfied.
skill.why_it_happens: Placement requires being at the target container and a successful put must be verified from the observation; otherwise the first item may still be held or not placed.
skill.how_to_avoid: Navigate to the destination before placing. After each put, inspect the observation to confirm success. If the put did not succeed, move to the target if needed and retry before starting the next search or placement cycle.

skill.description: Attempting to put an object into, or take an object from, a closed cabinet, drawer, or similar container may produce no effect. Conversely, if the container is already open, an open action returns 'Nothing happens' and should not be retried; proceed to put.
skill.why_it_happens: The environment requires the container to be open before its contents can be accessed or modified, and reports no change when opening an already-open container.
skill.how_to_avoid: Open the container first with the appropriate open action. If it is already open or open returns no effect, proceed directly to put rather than retrying open; after opening, verify access before taking or placing.

skill.description: Using an examine-style action on objects or locations is not supported and returns no useful information.
skill.why_it_happens: The available interaction set is limited to navigation, taking, putting, opening, and inventory-style operations; examining is not an effective substitute.
skill.how_to_avoid: Inspect a location by navigating to the receptacle and observing its contents. Pick up visible target objects with a take action from that receptacle.

skill.description: Placing an object into a non-target or unsuitable container such as a garbage can can make retrieval impossible or cause the overall two-item placement to fail.
skill.why_it_happens: Some containers may not accept objects cleanly, may change object state, or may not allow reliable retrieval; temporary storage is only safe if the object can be taken back.
skill.how_to_avoid: Prefer placing the first object directly into the final destination. If temporary holding is unavoidable, choose an open, stable, recoverable surface or container and avoid garbage cans or other likely irreversible containers.

skill.description: After several containers have been opened and no target found, repeatedly revisiting locations already confirmed empty can exhaust the action budget and cause failure.
skill.why_it_happens: Searching without tracking checked locations leads to redundant actions, while unchecked opened containers or visible surfaces may still contain the target.
skill.how_to_avoid: Maintain a mental or explicit list of checked locations. Prioritize unchecked opened containers and visible surfaces; take a target directly if it is visible. Avoid revisiting a location already confirmed to have no target unless new evidence suggests otherwise.

skill.description: Repeatedly declaring a subtask complete without executing the required next action can trigger a loop guard and terminate the episode before the two items are placed.
skill.why_it_happens: The current state may be misread as satisfying the completion condition even though the actual goal or subgoal is unfinished, causing repeated signals instead of progress.
skill.how_to_avoid: Signal completion only after the corresponding subgoal is actually achieved, such as an object being taken or placed. After signaling, continue with the necessary next action and avoid repeating the same completion signal without new progress.

skill.title: Search visible surfaces first and broaden across plausible locations
skill.principle: When a target object's location is unknown, locate it before manipulation by checking open, directly observable surfaces and common holding places first, such as tables, countertops, desks, dressers, shelves, beds, sofas, and chairs. Only then open closed containers such as drawers, cabinets, fridges, and microwaves. Treat the search as a broad multi-location search rather than assuming one named receptacle contains the object; if an early location is empty, broaden to other plausible unchecked locations.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target object's location is unknown at the start, or when the first checked location does not contain it.

skill.description: Failed searches often repeat the same empty surfaces or failed take attempts, or conclude the object is unavailable before all plausible open surfaces and relevant containers have been checked. A search should maintain a checked-location list and move to a new unchecked plausible location after a failed take.
skill.why_it_happens: The search may be treated as an unconstrained sequence without bookkeeping, so empty locations are revisited and some plausible locations are never examined.
skill.how_to_avoid: Record each checked location and its result. After a failed take or empty look, mark that location checked and move to another plausible unchecked location. Do not revisit confirmed empty surfaces unless the environment state changed. Open closed receptacles before treating them as searched and prioritize locations by object type. Search likely containers and surfaces; if the object remains absent after relevant locations are exhausted, report failure rather than continuing indefinitely.

skill.title: Open closed containers before taking or placing, and verify destination openability
skill.principle: When a closed drawer, cabinet, safe, fridge, microwave, or similar container may hold the target or is the placement destination, navigate to it and open it before attempting to take from it or put into it. Closed containers cannot be inspected or used directly. Before placing, confirm the destination is already open or can be opened; if opening returns no change, treat it as non-openable and choose a valid open destination or surface. For non-openable fixtures, use only a go-then-put sequence.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target may be inside a closed container, or when the placement destination is closed or its openability is uncertain.

skill.title: Navigate to the object and destination before take or put; proceed directly after acquisition
skill.principle: A take action succeeds only when the actor is at the receptacle where the object is present, and a put action succeeds only when the actor is at the destination. Locate and acquire the target object before traveling to the target container. Once the target is held, go directly to the specified destination and place it without unnecessary intermediate steps; if a put fails, verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying.
skill.when_to_apply: When retrieving an object whose location is not current, when moving a held object to a destination, or after a failed put.

skill.title: Use exact action forms, identifiers, and matching object types
skill.principle: Use the environment's supported action forms: go to a location, take an object from a receptacle, put an object in or on a receptacle, and open a container before accessing it. Refer to exact object and receptacle identifiers from observations, and track the specific instance taken so later actions use the same one. Do not use examine or open on non-container surfaces; open only applies to openable containers. Before taking or transforming, confirm the object name matches the goal, because similar but different objects may not satisfy it. If many containers have been checked without success, reassess visible surfaces and the target description rather than continuing blind exhaustive checks.
skill.when_to_apply: Throughout object search, retrieval, and placement, especially when forming commands or when an action seems unsupported or ambiguous.

skill.description: When an action such as go to, open, take, put, use, or clean returns 'Nothing happens', do not repeat the same command. Failed attempts can come from being at the wrong location, using an inexact or invalid identifier, targeting a closed or non-openable receptacle, or trying an inaccessible location. After a failed placement, verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying. Treat an unreachable navigation target as unavailable and switch to another candidate; treat an already-open container as open and continue rather than reopening it. Repeated no-change results are evidence that the current approach is exhausted.
skill.why_it_happens: The same invalid action may be retried without updating the inferred state, and a failed task segment may be reissued identically instead of changing the search location, object description, or strategy.
skill.how_to_avoid: After a no-change observation, re-check location, inventory, exact identifiers, and object or container state. Change at least one relevant condition: move to a different reachable location, open a closed container, use the specific instance id, or switch to another strategy. After one or two identical failures, stop retrying. If a task segment fails or returns without meeting its condition, do not repeat it unchanged; broaden the search or change the approach. Before declaring blocked, ensure every plausible closed container was actually opened and inspected, not merely approached, and avoid revisiting surfaces already confirmed empty.

skill.title: Use an acquire-then-operate sequence with explicit completion conditions
skill.principle: For tasks that require an object to be found and then manipulated, cleaned, heated, cooled, examined, or placed, split the task into an acquisition phase and an operation phase. The acquisition phase ends only when the target object is actually held, not merely seen or when a container is opened. The operation phase ends only when the environment observation confirms the required final state, such as the object being at the destination, cleaned, heated, or cooled. Begin placement only after acquisition is confirmed by holding the target object.
skill.when_to_apply: When a goal requires an object to be acquired before it is used, transformed, or placed, and the object is not already held.

skill.description: Do not declare completion or stop based on an attempted action alone. After critical actions such as take, put, clean, heat, or cool, inspect the observation for the goal predicate. Declare success only when the observation confirms the required final state; declare failure only when the observation shows an invalid or blocked action, an unreachable object, or exhaustion of plausible locations. If the placement observation already confirms the goal, treat it as terminal and do not run a redundant verification step.
skill.why_it_happens: Plans may assume an action succeeded without checking feedback, or may declare failure after a successful action sequence, or may add an unnecessary verification step after success, causing loops.
skill.how_to_avoid: After each critical action, compare the observation with the expected state. If the action failed, retry only after adjusting the approach; if it succeeded, stop issuing extra actions. Treat a confirming placement, cleaning, heating, or cooling observation as the terminal success condition. Do not declare completion before the final placement is confirmed; after confirmation, stop and do not send empty or inventory-only actions.

skill.title: Simple pick-and-place procedure
skill.principle: For simple pick-and-place goals, decompose the task into two ordered subtasks: first locate and take the target object, then move to the specified destination and put the object down.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal is to move a single object to a specified destination and no additional state change such as cleaning, heating, cooling, or lighting is required.

skill.title: 台灯观察：先取得目标物，再到台灯所在家具使用带编号台灯
skill.principle: 先确认目标物和台灯位置；台灯通常固定在家具表面。若目标物与台灯在同一表面被观察到，先 take 目标物，再使用带实例编号的 use desklamp <id>；不要在未持有目标物时先 use desklamp，否则常返回 Nothing happens。若目标物不在台灯处，先取得并携带目标物到承载台灯的家具。到达后使用 use desklamp <id> 触发观察；不要用裸名或复合语法，也不要把台灯当作可携带物或导航点。
skill.when_to_apply: 当任务要求 examine/look at 某物 with/under the desklamp，且环境中存在可交互的 desklamp 时。

skill.description: 多条失败轨迹显示，take desklamp、go to desklamp 或重复 go to 台灯/桌面通常返回 Nothing happens，浪费步骤并可能阻断后续观察。台灯是固定在家具上的交互点，不是可携带物或可导航位置。
skill.why_it_happens: 环境把台灯建模为固定光源或固定设备，只有其所在家具可作为导航目标，台灯本身不能作为 take 或 go to 的目标。
skill.how_to_avoid: 不要尝试拿取、移动或导航到台灯。先到达承载台灯的家具（desk、sidetable、dresser、coffeetable 等），在已到达后直接使用带编号的 use desklamp <id>；若已在台灯处，不要重复 go to 同一位置。

skill.description: Failed trajectories show that examine X with desklamp, examine on a location or object, examine desklamp, bare-name use desklamp, use desklamp on X, and use X on desklamp often return 'There's nothing special about X' or 'Nothing happens' and cannot substitute for the observation condition. Merely placing the target on the desk or desklamp without triggering the lamp interaction also leaves the goal unmet.
skill.why_it_happens: The environment does not support examine as a tool parameter for the lamp, does not support bare-name or compound use syntax, and does not treat placement as triggering the observation success condition. Examine on a location also returns no useful information.
skill.how_to_avoid: Locate and bring the target object to the lamp's furniture, then use the observed numbered lamp instance with use desklamp <id>. Do not use examine X with desklamp, examine a location, or compound use syntax; if an invalid form was tried, verify the lamp instance name and retry rather than repeatedly examining the target or lamp.

skill.description: 如果 use desklamp 返回 Nothing happens，通常说明当前不在台灯所在位置、当前家具观察中并无台灯，或交互条件未满足；同一位置重复同一 use/examine/look 指令不会改变状态，并可能形成循环或触发保护。连续一两次失败后应停止重复。
skill.why_it_happens: 使用台灯要求与台灯所在家具同处，且错误语法或位置不会产生状态变化；把空观察误当作可重试信号会重复无效动作。
skill.how_to_avoid: 失败后先核对当前家具观察中是否确实列出 desklamp；若没有，移动到已观察到台灯的其他家具，而不是重试同一 use。若台灯在场，确保目标物已取得或保持后改用带编号 use desklamp <id> 重试；若仍无变化，改为搜索其他位置或声明无法完成，不要重复相同指令。

skill.title: 台灯观察搜索策略：优先开放表面并系统检查容器
skill.principle: 搜索目标物或台灯时，优先检查与台灯相关的开放表面，如 desk、sidetable、床头柜、床、dresser、sofa、coffeetable 等；一旦观察到台灯，应直接前往其所在家具并在需要时使用台灯，不要继续遍历大量抽屉。若合理开放表面没有目标物，再按容器类型（drawer/cabinet）系统搜索，找到后返回台灯处。避免反复 look/examine 同一位置；没有新信息时转向其他家具或容器。'under the desklamp' 不保证目标物或台灯一定在假定位置，因此假定位置不可见时应搜索其他表面和容器。
skill.when_to_apply: 在台灯观察任务中寻找目标物或台灯，或已到达假定台灯位置但目标物或台灯不在该处、连续观察无新信息时。

skill.title: Clean-then-place ordered workflow with clean-state check
skill.principle: For goals requiring a clean object to be placed, execute distinct stages: locate and acquire the target object; bring it to a compatible cleaning fixture, preferring a sinkbasin; clean it; confirm from the observation that cleaning succeeded; then go to the destination, open it if closed, and place the object. Do not place before cleaning, and do not treat the clean step as done unless the observation confirms it. If cleaning has not succeeded, return to the cleaning stage before attempting placement.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal is to put a clean object in or on a specified receptacle and the object is not already clean.

skill.description: A clean action can return no effect when the object is not held or the current location is not a valid cleaning fixture. Cleaning is reliably supported at a sinkbasin; alternative fixtures such as bathtubbasin or fridge should not be assumed equivalent. Repeated identical attempts waste steps.
skill.why_it_happens: The environment validates that the object is held and that cleaning occurs at a compatible fixture; some fixtures or objects do not support cleaning.
skill.how_to_avoid: Hold the target object, navigate to a sinkbasin, then clean. If no effect, verify the held object and current location; try a different sinkbasin or confirm the object is cleanable. Treat bathtubbasin as unverified and switch to sinkbasin if it fails; do not loop on an invalid fixture.

skill.description: Certain objects such as towels or cloth may not support the clean action at a sinkbasin; repeated clean attempts fail. Prefer objects that are typically cleanable, and if a clean attempt fails, consider that the chosen object may be unsuitable.
skill.why_it_happens: Not every object type supports cleaning, or the selected object may not be the task's intended cleanable item.
skill.how_to_avoid: Before committing, select a likely cleanable candidate. If clean returns no effect after confirming the fixture and held object, try another candidate object or report the object as not cleanable rather than repeating the same action.

skill.description: Placement can fail when the destination container is closed, has no available space, or is not a valid receptacle; for example, some fixtures such as toilets or coffeemachines may reject placement. An open action may also return no effect if the container is already open or not openable.
skill.why_it_happens: Containers may require opening or have capacity limits; some fixtures are not valid placement targets. Repeating put or open without changing conditions may waste steps.
skill.how_to_avoid: Before placing, open a closed destination; if open returns no effect, treat it as already open or non-openable and proceed directly to put rather than retrying open. Check for space or availability when possible. If the destination is invalid or put repeatedly has no effect, seek an alternative valid destination or report blocked rather than looping.

skill.description: Goals name a specific object type. Similar alternatives, such as mug for cup, pan for pot, or butterknife for knife, should not be silently substituted. A close synonym may be considered only if the exact object is unavailable and the environment or observation explicitly treats it as equivalent or the goal permits it; otherwise continue searching or report the mismatch.
skill.why_it_happens: Generalizing categories can cause taking the wrong item and failing the task; conversely, exact-name matching may miss an accepted synonym, so equivalence must be confirmed rather than assumed.
skill.how_to_avoid: First search for the exact named type. If not found, do not swap in a different type by default; only use a confirmed equivalent. If the destination already contains a similar object, still acquire, clean, and place the correct target rather than swapping.

skill.description: Searching for the target object should prioritize plausible locations and avoid opening every remaining container indefinitely. If the object is not found after checking a reasonable set of likely locations, reassess or report blocked rather than continuing a step-consuming loop.
skill.why_it_happens: Item locations follow some regularities, but unusual placement or impossible tasks can occur; unbounded search wastes steps and can cause timeout or failure.
skill.how_to_avoid: Prioritize likely locations by object type: food-related items in fridge; dishes or utensils in countertop, cabinet, or drawer; cleaning supplies near sinkbasin, countertop, or shelf. After a few likely locations fail, consider unusual placement or impossibility, then reassess or report blocked rather than exhaustively opening all containers.

skill.title: End-to-end heat-then-place sequence
skill.principle: For a heat-then-place goal: locate and take the target object, go to the microwave, open it if closed, perform the heating operation using an observation-confirmed method, keep track of the same object instance, then go to the final destination, open it if needed, put the object there, and confirm placement. Treat heating as an intermediate milestone; the task is complete only after the object is placed at the destination. If the object is already held after acquisition, proceed to the heating stage rather than restarting unnecessarily.
skill.when_to_apply: Any task requiring an object to be heated and then placed at a specified destination.

skill.title: Microwave heating with observation-driven holding/placement recovery
skill.principle: Open the microwave before taking from or using it. Observations conflict on the required heating state: some successful runs heated the object while holding it, while others succeeded by placing the object in an open microwave and then heating. Treat the holding/placement requirement as observation-dependent. If heating while holding returns 'Nothing happens', place the object in the open microwave and retry. If heating with the object inside returns 'Nothing happens', take it out, ensure the microwave is open, and retry while holding it. Use the exact supported form heat <object> with microwave <id>; do not issue use <object> or heat <appliance>. Do not repeat an identical failing heat command without changing the object's position or holding state.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target object must be heated with a microwave, especially if the first heat attempt fails or the object is inside the microwave.

skill.description: A heat command can fail or return 'Nothing happens', and treating an unconfirmed attempt as success can lead to moving and placing a cold object. Do not infer heating success from merely holding or placing the object.
skill.why_it_happens: Heating may not change state unless the object’s position and the microwave state are suitable, and success is not guaranteed just because a command was issued.
skill.how_to_avoid: Proceed only after an explicit heating-success observation, such as a message that the object was heated, or another reliable confirmation that it is hot. If heating is not confirmed, repeat a valid heating attempt after correcting the object’s position or holding state, then verify again before moving it.

skill.description: After microwave heating returns 'Nothing happens', switching to stoveburners, toasters, or other appliances without evidence can also fail or be blocked. Assumption-based substitution adds failed steps rather than recovering the task.
skill.why_it_happens: Some appliances may not support heating the target object, some surfaces may be occupied, and support for a given object or appliance is not guaranteed merely because an alternative exists.
skill.how_to_avoid: Correct the microwave interaction first: check that it is open, adjust whether the object is held or placed inside, and retry without repeating the identical failing command. Use another appliance only when current observations explicitly show that it supports heating this object and is available; otherwise do not treat stoveburner or toaster as a blind fallback.

skill.title: Systematic search and continue after misses
skill.principle: When the target object is not in the first searched location, continue systematically checking other plausible containers and surfaces such as cabinets, drawers, countertops, fridge, dining table, sink basin, coffee machine, and stoveburners.
